title: Redwood discovery - Nova Retail latency & throughput
next_steps: Send token/sec benchmarking spreadsheet and sample prompt set
Share SOC 2 + ISO docs and KMS integration notes
Schedule 2-week dedicated capacity pilot for p95 150ms target
Follow up on network egress and VPC peering details
action_items: Emma Chen - Send pricing + bench spreadsheet - 2026-05-22
Luis Ortega - Prepare pilot run plan and reqs (GPU types, concurrency) - 2026-05-25
Raj Singh - Provide sample load and p95 targets per route - 2026-05-24
meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-20 | Time: 15:00-15:52 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Emma Chen, Luis Ortega, Priya Raman (Redwood) - Sofia Martinez, Raj Singh, Aisha Khan, Tom Lee (Nova Retail)
summary: Discovery to understand Nova Retail's latency/throughput SLOs for chat and streaming use cases. Customer currently evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; primary goals p95 latency ~150ms for 512-token streams at 8 concurrent users, peak concurrent 200 sessions for recommendation service. Security and VPC requirements discussed. Agreed to pilot dedicated capacity and run token/sec benchmarks.
transcript:
00:00:00 - Emma Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Emma from Redwood, AE on the account, with Luis and Priya. How's everyone doing?
00:00:08 - Sofia Martinez: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to dig into latency stuff.
00:00:15 - Luis Ortega: Cool, quick agenda. We want to cover current stack, latency targets (p95), concurrency, streaming behavior, and security constraints. Then propose next steps and a pilot.
00:00:28 - Tom Lee: Sounds good. We'll probably interrupt with product questions.
00:00:35 - Raj Singh: Quick context: we run a real-time product recommendations chat and an assistant. Currently on self-hosted Triton endpoints + a mix of CPU fallbacks. We're seeing 300-600ms median and p95 around 1.2s, which is too slow. Need to get p95 down to ~150-200ms for most requests.
00:01:02 - Priya Raman: Thanks Raj. Important to clarify workloads — are these full 2k-token completions or shorter streams?
00:01:12 - Raj Singh: Mostly streaming for assistant — typical turn 300-600 tokens, often 512 tokens max. For recommendations it's short prompts, 30-60 tokens but high QPS.
00:01:28 - Aisha Khan: Also note our infra: AWS us-east-1, VPC, we need SSM and KMS for key management, plus audit logs.
00:01:37 - Luis Ortega: Great — the two patterns change how we size. Streaming long sequences needs KV cache and efficient attention kernels; short QPS-heavy paths benefit a low-latency dedicated pool with batching disabled or micro-batching.
00:01:55 - Sofia Martinez: Our p95 target is 150ms for the short prompts, and 300ms p95 for 512-token streaming responses — is that realistic on hosted?
00:02:07 - Priya Raman: For hosted, we can hit sub-200ms p95 for short single-turn prompts on optimized models on our fastest nodes when concurrency is modest. For 512-token streaming, much of that is perceived latency because the stream emits first token quickly but tail latency depends on token/sec. We usually characterize streaming latency as time-to-first-token (TTFT) and per-token rate.
00:02:33 - Raj Singh: When you say per-token rate, what numbers do you see? tokens/sec?
00:02:38 - Luis Ortega: It depends on model and GPU. On an A100-like profile we see ~350-600 tokens/sec for medium models in optimized runtime; on H100 it's higher. For quantized 4-bit on Ampere variants it's a bit different. But critical is concurrency — if you have 200 concurrent sessions, tokens/sec per session drops unless we scale the pool or use dedicated capacity.
00:03:05 - Tom Lee: So for our recommendation micro-prompts (30 tokens), we need p95 150ms at 200 concurrent sessions — that's challenging.
00:03:13 - Priya Raman: Right. For that profile we recommend Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pool and predictably sized autoscaling. Also prefix caching for repeated prompts can help if prompts are similar.
00:03:28 - Sofia Martinez: Does dedicated mean on our VPC or still hosted in Redwood-managed infra?
00:03:34 - Emma Chen: Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware but isolated tenant pools. Private deployment is the VPC/on-prem option. For strict data residency and air-gap you pick Private. Dedicated gives predictability without you managing infra.
00:03:49 - Raj Singh: We probably want Dedicated to start, but we need SSO and audit logs.
00:03:55 - Aisha Khan: And KMS integration. Also need to know data retention and ability to disable logging for specific routes.
00:04:03 - Luis Ortega: We support KMS/HSM integrations for Private; for Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys via KMS in several options — we will share the security pack. You can also configure per-route logging.
00:04:18 - Sofia Martinez: Back to latency — can you run a head-to-head token/sec bench with our sample prompts?
00:04:24 - Priya Raman: Yes, we usually do a bench run. Typical deliverable is a token/sec spreadsheet and p95 breakdown by route, with concurrency swept.
00:04:33 - Raj Singh: Important: we need streaming behavior — time-to-first-token 60ms ideally and steady-state token/sec of ~200-400 depending on model.
00:04:44 - Luis Ortega: For TTFT 60ms you need fast networking, warm KV cache and micro-batching disabled. On our side we can prioritize warm paths, but network egress, TLS handshake and initial scheduling add overhead. If you colocate (VPC peering) to reduce hop count that helps.
00:05:02 - Tom Lee: Our infra team can do a VPC peer with a load balancer.
00:05:07 - Aisha Khan: Would we need a private endpoint for peering?
00:05:10 - Emma Chen: Yes, dedicated and private support private endpoints. We'll list the options in the security doc.
00:05:18 - 00:15:00 - [snip long technical back-and-forth, bench details referenced]
00:15:00 - Raj Singh: Can you explain fallbacks — if Dedicated pool is saturated what happens?
00:15:08 - Luis Ortega: We have routing policies: you can configure fallbacks to lower-cost variants or to hosted shared capacity. For customer-sensitive workloads you can set to fail closed. There's also auto-burst to shared capacity if you enable it.
00:15:22 - Sofia Martinez: Does that affect p95 calculations?
00:15:25 - Priya Raman: Yes — p95 may spike during fallback. Our recommend pilot will run with failover disabled to capture baseline, then with failover to see worst-case.
00:15:36 - Raj Singh: For the pilot, what inputs do you need from us?
00:15:40 - Luis Ortega: Sample prompt sets, model preference (we can suggest variants), target p95s by route, desired concurrency and any model quantization constraints. Also network diagrams for peering.
00:15:52 - Aisha Khan: We'll need an NDA addendum for security docs?
00:15:55 - Emma Chen: We can attach SOC2 and ISO docs under NDA. We'll send a link.
00:16:05 - Tom Lee: Any competitors we should be worried about offering similar low latency?
00:16:09 - Priya Raman: Some public clouds and Anthropic self-host offerings — but their latency profiles vary and many customers find dedicated pools with optimized kernels give better p95 at scale.
00:16:22 - Raj Singh: What about cost? If we need to reserve dedicated capacity for peak 200 concurrent sessions is that going to blow our budget?
00:16:29 - Luis Ortega: We do usage-based hosted, committed reserved for Dedicated. We'll send cost-model scenarios — often you offset cost with batching, caching, and quantization. The pricing spreadsheet will include expected unit costs for different configs.
00:16:44 - 00:25:00 - [some overlap, notes about tokenization differences and measurement methodology]
00:25:00 - Priya Raman: Pilot proposal: two-week dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool (we suggest 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs to start), run at your target concurrency, capture p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec, then iterate. We'll include both time-to-first-token and steady-state token/sec metrics.
00:25:20 - Sofia Martinez: 4 H100 seems reasonable to start. What kind of p95 should we expect for 30-token recommendation prompts at 200 concurrent?
00:25:28 - Luis Ortega: With that sizing and proper network peering we aim for p95 around 120-160ms for short prompts, assuming efficient scheduling and no heavy batching. We'll validate in the pilot.
00:25:40 - Raj Singh: And streaming 512-token assistant flows?
00:25:44 - Priya Raman: We'll measure TTFT and tokens/sec. Expect TTFT to be ~60-120ms and steady tokens/sec per session depending on model; aggregate throughput will need more GPUs to keep token/sec per session high.
00:25:58 - Aisha Khan: For the pilot, can we run in our VPC or do you need us to use your hosted endpoint?
00:26:04 - Emma Chen: For Dedicated pilot we can do private endpoint peering. For private deployment we'd be fully in your VPC. We'll capture both options in the plan.
00:26:14 - Tom Lee: Can you share previous benchmarks?
00:26:17 - Priya Raman: Yes I'll attach a sample benchmark doc that shows tokens/sec across GPUs, model variants, quantization states, and p95 under different concurrencies.
00:26:28 - 00:35:00 - [detailed run-of-show for pilot, discussion of instrumentation and tracing hooks]
00:35:00 - Raj Singh: A few gotchas — cold starts, model warm-up, and KV cache misses cause big latency spikes. We need to understand warm-up strategies.
00:35:10 - Luis Ortega: We pre-warm weights and maintain working sets; KV cache persistence across sessions is configurable. We'll provide warm-up scripts. Also advices to pin hot routes to a smaller pool for better cache locality.
00:35:29 - Sofia Martinez: Can you do A/B tests of different quantization levels?
00:35:33 - Priya Raman: Yes, Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and show tradeoffs on quality vs latency. We'll run quality regressions on your eval prompts.
00:35:44 - Aisha Khan: Security question again: how long are logs stored by default?
00:35:48 - Emma Chen: Default retention is 90 days on hosted; Dedicated can be configured and Private you control it. We'll include retention options.
00:35:58 - Tom Lee: Ok let's recap and next steps.
00:36:02 - Emma Chen: Recap: Redwood to send benchmarking spreadsheet, security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS notes), pilot plan with suggested GPU sizing and network peering steps, pricing scenarios. Nova provides sample prompts, target p95 by route, and network diagrams.
00:36:22 - Sofia Martinez: That works. Can we also get an example SLA for Dedicated?
00:36:26 - Luis Ortega: Yes, we'll include a sample SLA and uptime/latency targets.
00:36:31 - Raj Singh: Timeline — we'd like to start pilot by June 1 if possible.
00:36:36 - Priya Raman: We'll aim to have plan and docs to you by May 22 to hit June 1 start.
00:36:45 - 00:51:00 - [wrap-up, some side questions about SDKs and streaming APIs, minor transcription hiccups noted]
00:51:05 - Emma Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet.
00:51:10 - Sofia Martinez: Thanks.
00:51:13 - Raj Singh: Appreciate it.
00:51:17 - Aisha Khan: Bye.
00:51:20 - Tom Lee: Bye.
00:51:25 - [call ended]
